summary: Toru Sagara was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1941–1944). He held posts at Ibaraki University (~1951–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University (~1982–1992).

Toru Takahashi was a scholar in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne (D. Litt., attested 1996–2000), where he also served as an assistant (attested 1997–1998).
Toru Yagi is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He served as a professor at Osaka Gakuin University (attested 1996).
Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University from around 1967 to 1976 and later held a post there from around 1980 to 2017.

Toshifumi Goto is a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1982. He studied under Karl Hoffmann and Johanna Narten, among others, and held professorial posts at Osaka University and Tohoku University.
Toshihide Unebe is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Issai Funahashi. He served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1991).

Toshihiko Izutsu was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies who studied at Keio University. He held academic posts at Keio University (1937–1981), McGill University (1961, 1969–1975), and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (1975–1979).

Toshihiko Kimura is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963). He held posts at Tohoku University, Tokai Gakuin University (~1980), and Shitennoji University (~2011).
Toshihiro Wada is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981. He served as a professor at Nagoya University from around 1990 to 2019.

Toshiichi Endo is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Kelaniya and a doctoral thesis under Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (1995).

Toshikazu Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He served as a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011–2015) and became a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

Toshiki Osada is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1974–1978). He served as a professor at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2017) and held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts (~2017).

Toshinori Ochiai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held posts at Kacho Junior College (~1989–1996), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996), and the Institute for the Study of Ancient Manuscript Buddhist Canons (~2008).
Toshio Ando was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University from around 1930 to 1933. He held posts at Doho University and Otani University (~1956–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~2005–2012) and held research posts at Toyo University (~2015–2018) and Zhejiang University (~2018–2022).

Toshio Nagahiro was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1951–1969) and later as president of Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).

Toshio Sako is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and at Columbia University, where Alex Wayman supervised his doctoral work.

Toshio Yamazaki was an Indologist and historian. He held academic posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1949–1977), Chuo University (~1977–1987), Hannan University, and the University of Tokyo, where he was named professor emeritus.

Toshiya Unebe is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as an associate professor of Indian studies at Nagoya University (attested 2006–2011).
